chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is upon you to travel at night, for the earth is folded up at night.'
ai.seo_question: Why is it recommended to travel at night according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, highlights the physical ease of night travel due to the earth being 'folded' (tawq), a concept often interpreted by Shia scholars as a divine mercy reducing distance and fatigue. It serves as a practical guideline for travelers, emphasizing reliance on God's natural facilitation while also carrying spiritual undertones of seeking tranquility away from the day's distractions.

en.hubeali: H 14937 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nowfaly, from Al-Sakuny, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws has said:
‘The Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is on you to travel at night, for the ground folds up at night’.
en.sarwar: A number of our companions, Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ismail Bin Mahraan, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Basheer Al-Nabaal, from Humraan Bin Ayn who said: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s.), ‘The people are saying the earth would fold up for us at night, how it would fold up?’ He (a.s.) said: ‘Like this’, then folded his (a.s.) cloth’.
